doc.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The Village, Big Sur and leaving the business
title: Stepping out on a limb: UCLA sellout and the postage-stamp manager
summary: He tells of selling out Royce Hall twice in 1969 and of a manager promising a postage stamp, which he took as a sign to leave.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So I mean I’m sitting here today because some blessings. Because I didn’t orchestrate to be here. Cause if I had orchestrated to be here I would have stayed in there when they were gonna put me in arenas to make some bread. But when I left man, I stepped out on a limb.
It’s one of the most courageous things to say I’m gonna live where I want to live, instead of where the business is demanding that you live.

But then did you dig all them cats came out here, and they was telling me Charles... But I stepped out on a limb. Nobody was out there, I had no peers or nothing like that, you know. But here’s the thing... and then even then, cats would find me and bring blow and stuff to my pad and stuff like that. And I was living on the beach and stuff like that. I played at UCLA. I was out here on a tour, a forty one nighter on the West Coast. I was doing this before Flower days. And I had a concert at UCLA. It sold out just like that. Then they asked for another one that same night.
Wow.

Selling Royce Hall out twice? It don’t happen now! Think about that. This was ’69. So I’m out on a West Coast tour... This is deep. So I knew I was gonna make my getaway. Because I had been in Hong Kong, and I had a manager there who was twenty

years my senior. And someone asked him in Hong Kong - one of those palaces up on the hill looking at things - that, “What are you gonna do with Charles?” He said, “I’m gonna get him on a U.S. Postage Stamp.” So I got back and I went to my painter friend, Danny Johnson. He said, “What’s going on Charles?” I said, “My manager just said - among other things we were talking about - he’s gonna get me on a U.S. Postage Stamp.” He said, “Charles, you know what that means?” Do you know what it means?
Yeah.
Do you know what it means?
In my mind it means that he felt that he could get you to the point, but you’d have to sell out to get there.
No, no.
No, I got it wrong? Right.
You can’t be alive to be on a postage stamp.
Ahh!
The guy was twenty years my senior. How does that compute? Think about it. I knew then it was time for me to hack.
In other words...
Explain it to me.
You’re gone?
I think he saw you as a cash cow and he’s gonna work you.
I got it, I got it.
You’re talking to another peer of his and they said what are you gonna do it?
Yeah. Now that is heavy.
